summary: This Wikipedia article provides an overview of Houston, Texas, covering its rankings and reputation, airports, highway system, arts and theater scene, politics, geography and climate-related flooding, population and demographics, hurricane evacuations, government, geology, and the Texas Medical Center. It draws on census figures, surveys and media rankings to describe the city as the most populous in Texas and the fourth most populous in the United States.
one_line: Overview of Houston, Texas, covering its economy, transportation, arts, politics, geography, demographics, hurricanes, government, geology, and medical center.
key_facts: In 2008, Houston ranked top on Kiplinger's Personal Finance Best Cities of 2008 list.
William P. Hobby Airport was named Houston International Airport until 1967.
In 2015, Southwest Airlines launched service from a new international terminal at Hobby airport, the first international flights from Hobby since 1969.
Houston was incorporated in 1837 under the ward system of representation.
The MD Anderson Cancer Center has consistently ranked as one of the top two U.S. hospitals specializing in cancer care by U.S. News & World Report since 1990.
Interstate 610 encircles downtown with around an 8-mile (13 km) diameter, and Beltway 8 forms a middle loop at roughly 23 miles (37 km) in diameter.
In 2009, Houston became the first U.S. city with a population over 1 million to elect a gay mayor, Annise Parker.
The current mayor of Houston is Sylvester Turner, a Democrat elected on a nonpartisan ballot.
Houston is the most populous city in Texas and the fourth most populous city in the United States, with a census-estimated 2014 population of 2.239 million.
In August 2005, Houston became a shelter to more than 150,000 people from New Orleans who evacuated from Hurricane Katrina.
One month later, approximately 2.5 million Houston area residents evacuated when Hurricane Rita approached the Gulf Coast, the largest urban evacuation in U.S. history.
The Texas Medical Center employs more than 73,600 people and contains 49 member institutions, all non-profit organizations.
JPMorgan Chase Tower, completed in 1982, is Houston's tallest skyscraper at 1,002 feet (305 m) and the tallest structure in Texas.
Of the 10 most populous U.S. cities, Houston has the most total area of parks and green space, 56,405 acres (228 km2).
Houston is one of few United States cities with permanent, professional, resident companies in all major performing arts disciplines.
